title: IOM: Multi-Country Bundibugyo Ebola Virus Disease Outbreak - Situation Report No. 17 (31 August to 6 September 2026) - ReliefWeb

analysis.time: The situation report covers the period from 31 August to 6 September 2026, with the latest data as of 1 September 2026. The report was published on 11 September 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The outbreak is primarily in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), specifically in the provinces of Haut-Uélé and Bas-Uélé, which border the prefectures of Haut-Mbomou and Mbomou in the Central African Republic (CAR). It affects internally displaced persons (IDPs), mobile populations, and host communities in eastern DRC, including over 50 IOM-managed IDP sites in Ituri and North Kivu.
analysis.event: According to the Ministry of Health of the DRC, over 6,200 confirmed cases of Ebola disease caused by the Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) had been reported as of 1 September 2026, with more than 3,000 confirmed deaths. The outbreak is ongoing and poses a high risk of cross-border spread.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The outbreak has resulted in over 6,200 confirmed cases and more than 3,000 confirmed deaths. It is impacting IDPs, mobile populations, and host communities in eastern DRC. There is a high risk of cross-border transmission due to porous borders, informal crossings, and frequent population movements between DRC and neighboring countries such as Uganda, Tanzania, and CAR.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: IOM has scaled up its response, particularly at points of entry (PoEs), points of control (PoCs), and in displacement sites, to support enhanced surge capacity and coordination. Health operations are being expanded to detect, prevent, and respond to potential new cases. The situation remains under active investigation and monitoring.

analysis.brief_en: The IOM Situation Report No. 17 details a multi-country Bundibugyo Ebola Virus Disease (BVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), with data as of 1 September 2026. Over 6,200 confirmed cases and more than 3,000 confirmed deaths have been reported, primarily in the provinces of Haut-Uélé and Bas-Uélé, which border the Central African Republic (CAR). The outbreak is affecting internally displaced persons (IDPs), mobile populations, and host communities in eastern DRC, particularly in Ituri and North Kivu, where over 50 IOM-managed IDP sites are impacted. The report highlights the risk of cross-border spread due to porous borders and frequent population movements between DRC and neighboring countries like Uganda and Tanzania. IOM has intensified its response at points of entry (PoEs), points of control (PoCs), and displacement sites to enhance detection and prevention efforts. The outbreak remains under active investigation, with ongoing health operations aimed at mitigating further transmission.

The dashboard will be updated weekly to support EVD response efforts.
